title: Fast local clip search for score authoring
description:
## Intent
As a score-authoring agent working against a local Apricity library, I want to find usable clips quickly by my ratings, rating recency, and searchable clip/sample metadata, so I can shortlist sounds without loading the full catalog on every query.

## Scope
- Improve the local tools used by `.agents/skills/write-score` for rating-aware clip search.
- Use existing signals only: local stars and ratedAt, clip/sample names and paths, tags, kind, and duration where available. Keep current defaults compatible.
- Keep CLAP-based search outside this change.
- The public Clips page scan/infinite-scroll issue is diagnosed separately in the progress log; this work targets local score-authoring tools.

## Definition of done
- The ratings-aware local clip listing avoids reading every Clip record when only a small set is rated.
- Agents can sort by rating or rating recency and narrow results by text query and minimum stars.
- Output remains ready to paste into a score and makes the available signals visible.
- Add behavior coverage for default ordering, recency ordering, filtering, and missing records.
- Update the score-authoring skill with the useful invocation.
- Record verification and outcomes here.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Verified from the page code and schema: the UI already lazily constructs 24 cards through feedGrid/IntersectionObserver, but it first calls api.clips() and materializes the complete list. Clip has no library-wide GSI; its GSIs are sampleId/copyOf/candidateId. Amplify Clip.list therefore uses a table Scan, and listAll follows nextToken until the entire table is returned. Additionally, Catalog.clips() first awaits load(), whose library index performs a full Clip.list scan for counts, then performs a second full Clip.list scan for clip details. The broad design/scale.md explicitly deferred a Ranked-backed paginated Clips tab because top ranking, search, Mine, and clip filters currently depend on the full set. Current live page remained on Loading… while inspected. Next: decide and implement the paged ranked-list path (with visibility/filter semantics and backfill), or treat this as a diagnostic report.
